name: The National WWII Museum
unique: A vast museum with a restored Higgins boat, a Sherman tank, a 4D theater and the personal stories of the war in Europe and the Pacific.
buzz: One of the best museums in the country, and it takes most of a day. Start with the film and the train car.

name: City Park
unique: A 1,300 acre park with live oaks, a sculpture garden, a children's amusement park, a botanical garden and paddle boats on a lagoon.
buzz: The sculpture garden is free and the oaks are magnificent. Rent a bike or a boat.

name: St. Louis Cemetery No. 1
unique: The oldest cemetery in the city, with above ground tombs, the grave of Marie Laveau and a maze of family vaults.
buzz: You can only enter with a guide now, and the history of the burial customs is the point. Book ahead.

name: Frenchmen Street
unique: A strip of live music clubs, bars and restaurants just outside the French Quarter, where locals go to hear brass, funk and jazz.
buzz: The clubs are close together and the cover charges are low. Start early and follow your ears.

name: Mardi Gras World
unique: The warehouse where parade floats are built, with giant figures, props and a tour through the painting and sculpting shops.
buzz: The scale of the floats is the fun and kids love it. The tour includes a slice of king cake.

name: USS Kidd
unique: A World War II destroyer docked on the Mississippi, restored and open for self guided tours through the decks and turrets.
buzz: The ship is tight and real, and the museum explains the Pacific war. Good for kids who like machines.

name: LSU Rural Life Museum
unique: A 450 acre museum of Louisiana rural life with a plantation complex, slave cabins, a country store and farm equipment.
buzz: The slave cabins and the working farm are the powerful parts. The grounds are shady and quiet.

name: Louisiana State Capitol
unique: The tallest state capitol in the country, with an Art Deco interior, a observation deck and the spot where Huey Long was shot.
buzz: The observation deck view is the reason, and the building is a monument to Long's ambition. Free.

name: Vermilionville
unique: A living history village of Acadian, Creole and Native American houses on the bayou, with music, cooking and craft demonstrations.
buzz: The music and food demos are the best part, and the village is shady and walkable. Good for kids.

name: Natchitoches Historic District
unique: The oldest settlement in Louisiana, with a brick main street, a river walk, a fort site and 18th century houses.
buzz: The river street is the photo and the meat pies are the local food. Christmas lights are a big draw.

name: Sci-Port Discovery Center
unique: A hands on science center with a planetarium, an IMAX, a space exhibit and a toddler area on the Shreveport riverfront.
buzz: Good for a rainy day with kids, with enough to fill an afternoon. The planetarium is a bonus.

name: Biedenharn Museum and Gardens
unique: The home of the first bottler of Coca-Cola, with the original bottling plant, a museum and formal gardens.
buzz: The bottling equipment and the family story are the interesting parts. The gardens are a bonus.

name: Southdown Plantation
unique: A 1859 sugar plantation house with a museum of the sugar industry, the enslaved workers and the Cajun culture that followed.
buzz: The sugar history is well told and the house is handsome. Check hours before driving out.

name: Los Islenos Museum
unique: A museum of the Canary Islanders who settled the parish in the 1770s, with a village, a church and the story of the 2005 flood.
buzz: The Isleno history is unique and the flood exhibit is moving. Free.

name: Madewood Plantation
unique: A Greek Revival mansion on Bayou Lafourche, still family owned and open for tours and overnight stays.
buzz: The house is stunning and the family story is personal. Book ahead for a tour or a night.

name: Fort Jackson
unique: A brick fort on the Mississippi below New Orleans, used in the Civil War and later as a prison, with a moat and a river view.
buzz: The fort is weathered and quiet, and the river is right there. A good stop on the way to the delta.

name: Abbeville Shrimp Festival
unique: A street festival in the shrimp capital of Louisiana, with boiled shrimp, gumbo, music and a parade.
buzz: The food is the point and the shrimp are fresh. Go early for parking.

name: Brownell Memorial Park
unique: A small park with a 100 foot observation tower, a cypress swamp and a rookery full of egrets and herons.
buzz: The tower gives a canopy view of the swamp and the birds are close. Free.
